patches.old: Drive-reduction theory, developed by Hull and rooted in Hullian homeostasis, proposes that biological needs (like hunger) create uncomfortable psychological states called drives
patches.new: Drive-reduction theory, developed by Hull and built on Cannon's concept of homeostasis, proposes that biological needs (like hunger) create uncomfortable psychological states called drives

sources.title: OpenStax, Psychology 2e §10.1 — motivation, covering instinct theory, drive reduction, arousal theory and the Yerkes-Dodson relationship between task difficulty and optimal arousal

visual.title: The two Yerkes-Dodson curves and Hull's product
visual.alt: Two inverted-U curves of performance against arousal, the complex-task curve peaking at lower arousal and the simple-task curve peaking at higher arousal; Hull's equation with drive, habit strength and incentive explained and the note that any term at zero abolishes behaviour; and three cards summarising instinct, drive-reduction and arousal theory with the weakness that undid each.
visual.caption: The second half of the law is the half students drop: the peak itself slides left as the task gets harder.
